summary: Historical response, execution and usage projections join native invocations and expose attempt and invocation groupings

replay.detail: Historical observations without an exact invocation or claim retain unknown joins. Current ownership is not backfilled into prior responses.

schema.detail: Adds optional invocation_id and attempt metadata to response rollups, usage rows and response attribution; step executions expose optional invocation_id. Existing execution spend remains the accounting authority.

rules.detail: Response attribution uses exact incarnation and historical claim lifecycle at response completion. Multiple active claims remain ambiguous. Usage partitions preserve claim identities and CLI/TUI views can group by step-scoped attempt or invocation.

compatibility.detail: Optional metadata is additive; legacy responses retain unknown execution, invocation and attempt. A verified launch alone does not prove later work ownership. Identity-only responses do not manufacture usage or zero cost.

downtime.detail: No fleet operation or new spend-table migration is required.

manual.detail: Existing usage queries retain their time-window contract; consumers may use the additional optional grouping keys.

recovery.detail: Durable response rollups preserve joins through timeline retention and failures without depending on sampled trace export.
